subject: Getting Error in unserialize(m) : unknown input format in hdfs.read

messages.author: 22583a676ffdcbde
messages.subject: Getting Error in unserialize(m) : unknown input format in hdfs.read
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to read the hdfs file content through rhdfs package. I have the below sample code to read the file content. While unserialize the data it throws "Error in unserialize(m) : unknown input format" error.

f = hdfs.file("/taqdata/drac-us-trade-v2-1/20120104/ADM.csv.gz","r")
m = hdfs.read(f)
model <- unserialize(m)

I appreciate your support.

Regards,
Thirumal Raman

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#525] Re: Getting Error in unserialize(m) : unknown input format in hdfs.read
parts: Yes, it's because it's compressed. How can unserialize decompress it? You can only call unserialize on data generated with serialize. It isn't a universal binary format decoder.

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#528] Re: Getting Error in unserialize(m) : unknown input format in hdfs.read
parts:
On Feb 12, 2013 10:57 PM, "Thirumal Raman" <r.thi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> To add upon, I understand that from.dfs internally uses hdfs.read to read the file content.
Check your sources. There is no dependency between rmr2 and rhdfs, hence what you are saying is not possible, and the source code is for everyone to see.
> The same files I was able to read it with from.dfs. I have one more point to see that the from.dfs taking around 7 secs to read the few kb file. Is it the performance bottleneck for from.dfs?

It is not meant to read efficiently puny files. The idea is that you would call from.dfs to get the results of a map reduce computation. If you need to read many small files one at a time you are looking into the wrong library.

Antonio
